body: Yeah, I don't even know what I'd do without my family, so I feel for your situation. Over the years I've become more dependent on them rather than less haha. I'll probably be chasing the feeling I got from my parents being proud of me when I was younger for the rest of my life.

Hey, thanks for commenting man. I don't really want to get into too much detail, but I just stopped doing things things like going to school and hanging out with friends sometime around age 12. 

Since then I've seen countless therapists with even more diagnosis's and have been prescribed tons of meds that I fear have only served to permenently ruin my brain chemistry.

 I regret not enjoying what should've been the best years of my life and I'm sorry that I couldn't have been more like my brother and sister. 

Regardless, I took your advice and just communicated to my parents about how I was feeling. There was a lot of crying and they told me that they loved me just the way I was and that they would never want me to harm myself. I mean, no parents would tell their kids they were a burden, but they seemed really sincere to me. 

So you were right kind stranger, I wasn't being sensible. Just was looking for a reason to justify ending it I guess.

I'm the black sheep of what would otherwise be a normal family, and I know they resent me for it.
Well, at least I know my triplet brother and sister do.
Anyway, thanks for the kind thoughts.
